research.abstract: ABSTRACT Bats are major reservoirs of emerging viruses, including severe acute respiratory syndrome‐related coronaviruses, yet they exhibit remarkable tolerance to viral infections with limited clinical manifestations‐a longstanding immunological paradox. Here, we generate a telomere‐to‐telomere (T2T) de novo genome assembly for Rhinolophus sinicus ( R. sinicus ), designated T2T‐RSC1.0 (2.14 Gb), comprising 17 fully anchored autosomes and both sex chromosomes. This gapless assembly resolves 129.19 Mb of previously unresolved regions (PURs) and enables annotation of 848 previously unannotated genes, including 131 protein‐coding genes and five pseudogenes on the 33.75 Mb Y chromosome. Using 2.12 × 10 5 newly identified single‐nucleotide polymorphisms within PURs, population genomic analyses resolve three major genetic groups and provide improved resolution of genome‐wide population structure. Comparative analyses further reveal population‐level associations between major histocompatibility complex polymorphism and viral diversity. Multi‐omics and functional analyses reveal a coordinated evolutionary remodeling of antiviral defense, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling, and inflammatory regulation in horseshoe bats. This study provides an unparalleled genomic resource for R. sinicus and establishes an integrated framework for investigating immune evolution, long‐term host–virus coexistence, and mammalian adaptive evolution.

research.abstract: Background Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is the leading cause of fatal atherothrombotic events, including myocardial infarction. Intimal microcalcification is a major determinant of plaque instability, but its pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly understood. The nuclear receptor Rev-erb-alpha regulates lipoprotein metabolism and inflammation. We hypothesized that it modulates atherogenesis by also controlling arterial calcification. Methods To identify regulators of vascular calcification, transcriptomic analysis of CD14+CD16- monocytes from diabetic patients with different calcium scores (ANGIOSAFE cohort) was combined with targeted analysis in calcified and non-calcified atherosclerotic plaques from diabetic and non-diabetic patients (AtheroPortal cohort) and in calcified and non-calcified areas of human endarterectomies isolated by laser capture microdissection (OPAL Cohort). Functional relevance was evaluated in 18-month-old Ldlr-/- mouse and in primary aortic vascular smooth muscle cells after targeting Rev-erb-alpha. Results In ANGIOSAFE (n=668), REV-ERB-alpha expression was lower in classical CD14+CD16- monocytes from diabetic patients with low coronary artery calcium scores. In the AtheroPortal cohort (n=968), REV-ERB-alpha expression was reduced in highly calcified plaques from diabetic patients, and laser capture microdissection confirmed lower expression in calcified compared to non-calcified areas of human endarterectomies. Rev-erb alpha-deficient Ldlr-/- mice displayed accelerated atherogenesis and calcification, with SMCs reprogrammed toward an osteochondroblastic phenotype. In vitro, Rev-erb-alpha preserved SMC identity by repressing IL-1-beta-driven transdifferentiation, notably via Spp1, Osterix and Sox9, and repressed the hyaluronidase Cemip, whose activity degrades hyaluronic acid and promotes intimal calcification. Conclusions Rev-erb-alpha restrains SMC-driven vascular calcification by suppressing osteogenic reprogramming, and may represent a therapeutic target to reduce calcification and cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. Here, we analysed 595 genomes of S. Typhimurium representing three food animal sources (bovine, swine, and poultry) and one non‐food animal source (wild birds). We found that S. Typhimurium from food animal sources generally had a more open pangenome and harboured more antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Notably, swine isolates exhibited the most open pangenome and the highest prevalence of ARGs, patterns that were associated with a greater presence of mobile genetic elements, particularly plasmids. Despite similar core genome sizes, S. Typhimurium from different sources displayed distinct patterns of positive selection in the core genome that varied in frequency and targeted functional categories. In contrast, although accessory genome sizes varied substantially across sources, the frequency of positive selection remained similar. Using machine learning, we identified source‐predictive genetic variants, many of which are associated with stress‐response functions. These findings suggest that gain and loss of accessory genes and positive selection acting on core genes support differential adaptation in S. Typhimurium, potentially contributing to its broad ecological range.

research.abstract: Background: Although direct-acting antivirals have transformed hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, 25-30% of active infections in Spain remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model to identify undiagnosed HCV infection using only data already recorded within the health system. Materials and Methods: We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study using the Andalusian Population Health Database (BPS). Individuals diagnosed with HCV between 2017 and 2024 (n=25,028) were matched, up to 10:1, to controls by birth year, sex, and health district. An Explainable Boosting Machine was trained on 2017-2022 data, with a threshold set in a 2023 validation set to guarantee [≥]60% sensitivity, then evaluated unmodified in an independent, non-matched, population-representative 2024 sample approximating real-world screening. Predictors comprised chronic-disease diagnoses and laboratory summary statistics recorded [≥]30 days before the index date; age and sex were excluded as matching variables. Predictors reflecting socioeconomic proxies or matching artefacts (pharmaceutical co-payment category, a zone-level deprivation index) were removed after explainability review. Results: In the independent test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (0.826 in validation), sensitivity 63.5%, specificity 91.8%, positive predictive value 7.0%, and negative predictive value 99.6%. Leading predictors were minimum alanine aminotransferase, HIV infection, dependence on non-tobacco substances, and platelet-count statistics, forming a clinically coherent, laboratory- and comorbidity-driven profile. Conclusion: An explainable model built exclusively from routine electronic health record data can identify undiagnosed HCV infection with discrimination comparable to previously published tools, evaluated under conditions approximating true population prevalence. Bias-auditing was feasible without sacrificing interpretability, supporting a scalable, equity-conscious instrument for the final phase of HCV elimination.

research.abstract: Estimating the effective sample size (ESS) is fundamental in Bayesian phylogenetic inference to account for autocorrelation in MCMC samples. While methods for continuous parameters are well established, the discrete and high-dimensional nature of treespace poses substantial challenges. In this paper, we introduce a new approach based on Conditional Clade Distributions (CCDs) to emulate MCMC chains with known ESS bounds. We compare existing tree ESS estimators with novel approaches that utilize CCDs as tractable tree distributions, as well as a new probabilistic estimator based on differences in clade frequencies between independent chains. Using our emulated chains from both simulated and real datasets, we assess estimators for their ability to recover the true ESS (accuracy), their insensitivity to the removal of autocorrelated samples from the chain (stability), and their tolerance to combining multiple chains together (robustness). We further examine how multimodality and poor inter-mode chain mixing can compromise the reliability of tree ESS estimates. These findings indicate that our new CCD-based estimators perform comparably to existing approaches with respect to accuracy, stability, and robustness. In contrast, the probabilistic estimator and two previously recommended methods incur prohibitive computational costs for long chains. Together, these results establish a new framework for evaluating tree ESS estimators using CCD-based emulated MCMC chains and demonstrate their performance and current limitations in practical phylogenetic analyses. The expanded suite of tree ESS estimators is available in the user-friendly TreeStat2 software package for BEAST 2.

research.abstract: Southeast Asia is home to 22 endemic raptors, and almost all are classified as “Endangered” or higher by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN). The limited range and fragmented distribution of some Southeast Asian raptors from the genus Nisaetus hinder the characterization of these endangered birds. This study presents the mitochondrial sequences of the Pinsker’s Hawk-eagle ( Nisaetus pinskeri ) and Changeable Hawk-eagle ( Nisaetus cirrhatus ) and conducts a comparative mitogenome analysis across Accipitriformes. The partial mitogenome lengths of N. pinskeri and N. cirrhatus are 18,654 bp and 17,874 bp, with a GC content of 46.4% and 47.4%, respectively. An extra cytosine at position 174 of the nad3 gene was present in both mitogenomes, which was not previously observed in other Nisaetus species. Phylogenetic analysis recapitulated the topology of the order Accipitriformes. It showed that N. pinskeri and N. cirrhatus are closely related to each other and sister to the rest of the Nisaetus representatives. Moreover, the trees based on concatenated mitochondrial protein-coding genes were closer to the latest reported phylogenies than single-gene trees using conventional mitochondrial markers. The selection pressure analysis showed that all protein-coding genes experienced purifying selection, with the highest in atp8 and the lowest in cox1 . As the first report of the near-complete mitogenomes of these raptors, this study expands the available genomic resources for these understudied raptors and provides a foundation for future population genetic research.

research.abstract: Abstract Importance Severe maternal morbidity is increasingly driven by chronic conditions present before pregnancy, but existing obstetric comorbidity indices rely on clinician documentation and are not designed for preconception use. Objective To determine whether conditions represented in a patient-facing preconception assessment are associated with severe maternal morbidity comparably with clinician-derived indices. Design Retrospective cohort study of deliveries from 1992 to 2025; scores were derived from diagnoses recorded at least 280 days before delivery. Setting Two deidentified electronic health record databases covering an academic and public health system in San Francisco and 5 other University of California medical centers. Participants Birthing individuals aged 12 to 55 years at delivery with at least 10 clinical events recorded before conception. Exposures Preconception Medical Assessment (PreMA) score (range, 0-8) and the Bateman (range, 0-51) and Leonard (range, 0-281) obstetric comorbidity indices, modeled per 1-SD increase. Main Outcomes and Measures Severe maternal morbidity and nontransfusion severe maternal morbidity within 7 days of delivery, defined by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention indicators. Results Among 58,549 deliveries (21,427 in the San Francisco cohort [mean (SD) maternal age, 33.4 (5.7) years]; 37,122 in the statewide cohort [33.1 (5.4) years]), each 1-SD increase in PreMA score was associated with severe maternal morbidity in the San Francisco cohort (relative risk [RR], 1.23; 95% CI, 1.19-1.28), similar to the Bateman (RR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.22-1.29) and Leonard (RR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.23-1.30) indices; statewide findings were consistent. Severe maternal morbidity rose from 6.6% at a score of 0 to 9.0% at 1 to 3 and 17.8% at 4 or greater (statewide, 3.8%, 5.3%, and 14.5%). Associations persisted across racial, ethnic, and neighborhood deprivation subgroups. Cardiovascular conditions (RR, 3.08; 95% CI, 2.50-3.80) and diabetes (RR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.34-2.48) were most strongly associated with nontransfusion severe maternal morbidity. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, higher scores on a patient-facing preconception assessment were associated with severe maternal morbidity, comparably with clinician-derived indices. Prospective studies are needed before scores are used clinically. Key Points Question Is a brief patient-completed preconception assessment associated with severe maternal morbidity? Findings In this study of 58,549 deliveries across two California health systems, each standard deviation increase in the electronic health record-derived Preconception Medical Assessment score was significantly associated with severe maternal morbidity, with a magnitude similar to two established clinician-facing comorbidity indices. Severe maternal morbidity ranged from 6.6% among deliveries with a score of 0 to 17.8% among those scoring 4 or greater. Meaning Conditions captured by this patient-completed assessment may identify candidates for preconception counseling and chronic disease optimization.

research.abstract: Abstract Phylogenetic analyses of molecular evolution often require repeated manual preparation to reconcile taxa, annotate trees, execute models, and summarize results. These steps become increasingly time-consuming and difficult to standardize as the number of taxa, genes, and analytical hypotheses increases. We present HYphlow, an open-source graphical workflow developed in Python that integrates data preparation, trait-based foreground branch assignment, HyPhy execution, and structured result extraction within a single interface. HYphlow reconciles taxon labels across alignments, trees, and trait data; reconstructs ancestral states using parsimony and maximum likelihood; generates alternative foreground annotations; executes HyPhy analyses locally or through portable scripts for high-performance computing; and records analytical decisions and settings throughout the workflow. We evaluated HYphlow using simulations and two published datasets comprising cryptochrome analyses in pigeons and doves and visual opsin analyses in skinks. A name-similarity threshold of 80 reliably recovered simulated spelling variants, while consensus foreground assignment increased precision relative to parsimony or maximum likelihood alone (0.928 vs 0.891 and 0.907, respectively), with a corresponding reduction in recall (0.875 vs 0.921 and 0.918). In the empirical datasets, HYphlow reconciled taxon labels, reconstructed or reproduced foreground hypotheses derived using different approaches, and generated selection results consistent with the principal conclusions of the original studies. HYphlow therefore provides a reproducible framework for carrying comparative molecular evolutionary analyses from independently prepared sequence, phylogenetic, and trait data through branch assignment, model execution, and results summary while retaining researcher control over analytical decisions. HYphlow is freely available under the MIT licence from GitHub at: https://github.com/Schott-Lab/HYphlow .

research.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 has adapted continuously since 2019, yet no multi-parameter framework has characterized this trajectory across geographically distinct United States populations. We present a systematic 13-parameter analysis of 137,059 high-quality genomes from ten diverse US states across three phases: pre-vaccination (January-December 2020), early vaccination (January-June 2021), and sustained immune pressure (July 2021-December 2025), the latter dominated by the high-volume Delta period with an early-Omicron contribution. Approximately 5000 genomes were retrieved per state per phase from GISAID EpiCoV under stringent quality filters, and each phase dataset was partitioned into three subsets, giving 90 subsamples in total, to quantify subsampling stability. Parameters spanned genome-wide mutation rate, dN/dS and Ti/Tv, site-specific selection (HyPhy FUBAR), spike and ACE2 contact-residue profiling, insertion-deletion characterization, furin cleavage site evolution, N-linked glycosylation dynamics, lineage-mutation concordance, amino acid physicochemical shifts, and protein-wise dN/dS ranking and mutation load. Genome-wide mutation rate rose monotonically in all ten states, from 0.050% to 0.149%, and dN/dS rose from 0.611 to 1.103, crossing neutrality in nine of ten states by Phase 3. Amino acid mutation load increased 3.95-fold, from 9.12 to 36.03 substitutions per sequence, while Ti/Tv fell from 3.69 to 2.11. Spike position 142 was diversifying in all ten states in Phase 3, with positions 484, 452, and 478 recurring in 70, 60, and 60 percent of states. ORF8 followed a spike-then-collapse trajectory (dN/dS 3.43, 14.23, 1.01), consistent with progressive loss of function. The reproducibility of these effects across ten geographically distinct state populations establishes a state-level baseline for SARS-CoV-2 immune escape.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bedaquiline (BDQ), pretomanid (Pa) and linezolid (LZD)-based (BPaL) regimens have transformed rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) treatment. However, resistance to these drugs is increasingly reported, while longitudinal data integrating clinical, phenotypic and genomic evolution remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a fatal case of recurrent RR-TB in a 40-year-old South African woman with HIV infection who received BPaL therapy. Following treatment completion, recurrent disease was complicated by pregnancy, treatment interruption and loss to follow-up. She subsequently re-presented with advanced cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis and respiratory failure. Despite re-initiation of BPaL, she deteriorated and died from septic shock. Routine drug susceptibility testing, available posthumously, confirmed resistance to BDQ, Pa and LZD. Seven sequential Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates collected during treatment underwent minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing and whole-genome sequencing. All demonstrated phenotypic resistance to the three BPaL drugs. Serial genomic analysis identified progressive Rv0678 diversification associated with a two-fold increase in BDQ MIC, while resistance-associated rrl and fbiC mutations remained comparatively stable despite persistently elevated LZD and Pa MICs. CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates the interaction of treatment interruption, delayed resistance detection and continued within-host bacterial adaptation during BPaL therapy. Longitudinal phenotypic and genomic findings revealed distinct resistance trajectories among BPaL drugs, highlighting the importance of treatment retention, timely susceptibility testing and genomic surveillance for preserving BPaL effectiveness.

research.abstract: Abstract Collagen is the most abundant protein in animals. Its thermal stability depends on its specific amino acid composition within the repeated Gly- Xaa -Y aa motifs forming the triple helix structure. Proline increases collagen rigidity, while serine enhances its elasticity—properties that contribute to collagen function and that vary with temperature. Although variation in collagen composition has been linked to temperature adaptation across evolutionary distinct taxa, its role within a species remains unclear. Here, we tested whether collagen genes across populations of the freshwater crustacean, Daphnia magna , show a signature of local adaptation to the ambient temperature. Analysing 39 collagen genes from 215 D. magna populations across three phylogeographic lineages spawning four continents, we found that animals from populations in warmer climates have higher proline and lower serine content in collagen—consistent with enhanced protein stability at higher temperatures. This variation was also associated with experimentally measured upper temperature tolerance. Parallel directional patterns of amino acid change appeared across genetically distinct lineages. Collagen genes also showed strong signatures of positive selection, comparable to that of immune-related genes, supporting a scenario of polygenic molecular role in adaptive responses. Our findings provide evidence of intraspecific molecular evolution in collagen amino acid composition driven by environmental temperature. Additionally, our study bridges macroevolutionary patterns with microevolutionary processes, posing the first intraspecific evidence that collagen genes can contribute to responses to environmental gradients at the molecular level, and thus, advancing our understanding of molecular adaptation of constrained structural proteins in an environmental context.

research.abstract: DEG (Degradation of periplasmic proteins) proteases are ATP-independent serine endopeptidases found in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes including plants. They are considered to be key regulators of development and stress tolerance in plants. In this study, a comprehensive genome-wide analysis identified 19 serine protease-like DEG family proteins in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.), revealing their structural diversity, domain architecture, and regulatory potential. Physiochemical profiling showed a predominance of acidic isoelectric points (pI), variable protein lengths (169–1083 amino acids), and differential stability indices. Subcellular localization predicted most DEG proteases to reside in the chloroplast, with others distributed across cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, and peroxisome. Domain analysis confirmed the universal presence of the trypsin domain, with varying numbers of PDZ domains and additional conserved motifs among paralogs. Evolutionary divergence analysis of StDEG genes and their orthologs from six Solanaceae species as well as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays revealed dN/dS ratios below one for all orthologous pairs, suggesting that StDEG genes have evolved under strong purifying selection and remained highly conserved throughout plant evolution. Gene ontology annotations linked DEG proteases to key biological functions including PSII repair, photoinhibition, and chloroplast organization, alongside protein catabolism and light stimulus response. Promoter analysis revealed an abundance of cis-regulatory elements (CREs), particularly light-responsive motifs, along with hormone and stress-related elements such as ABRE, ARE, and MBS. Expression profiling across eight developmental tissues demonstrated tissue-specific expression patterns, with strong transcript accumulation of selected DEG members in senescent leaf, stolon, shoot apex, and tuber. Interestingly, several splice variants showed unique expression dynamics, including stage-specific and stress-induced activation. Upon exposure to abiotic and hormonal cues, 16 DEG proteases displayed significant transcriptional modulation, particularly under light, ABA, and Zeatin treatments, with notable fold changes reaching up to 26-fold in certain variants. These findings highlight the functional versatility of DEG proteases in potato development and stress adaptation, especially their responsiveness to light and hormonal stimuli. The characterization of these proteases paves the way for future studies on their roles in crop resilience and genome editing applications.

research.abstract: A bstract Understanding the mechanisms facilitating the repeated evolution of traits is a core question in evolutionary biology. While repeated evolution has been observed across many systems, behavioral phenotypes have been less well studied than morphological traits. Migration is a behavioral adaptation to seasonality that has evolved independently in many animals, and repeated gains and losses of migratory behavior have been especially prevalent throughout the diversification of birds. While migratory traits are heritable in many taxa and candidate genes underlying intraspecific variation in migratory behavior have been identified, whether similar genetic changes are responsible for the repeated evolution of migration remains poorly understood. We used a phylogenomic approach to investigate the relationship between variation in candidate genes and migratory propensity across nearly all species in the parulid warbler radiation ( n = 101), a group of songbirds in which migratory behavior has been lost and gained multiple times. Comparisons of candidate gene tree topologies to the parulid warbler species tree revealed cases of discordance, though these were explained by differences in the number of phylogenetically informative sites among genes rather than by elevated genetic similarity among species sharing migratory strategies. Testing models of coding sequence evolution identified sites with elevated dN/dS in five candidate genes, suggestive of positive selection; however, variation at these sites showed no clear association with migratory strategy, nor did we detect recurrent selection across lineages where transitions in migratory behavior most likely occurred. Together, these results contradict the hypothesis that selection on shared variation (ancestral polymorphisms or introgressed alleles) facilitated the repeated evolution of migration in this clade.

We recovered ancient DNA from 2,600-year-old microfauna and historical museum specimens to investigate the island’s extinct fauna. Despite challenging preservation conditions, we successfully recovered mitogenomes from historical Vipera latastei specimens, and partial mitogenomes from snake, skink, and lizard subfossils. Phylogenetic analyses confirm the extinct Columbretes snake as Vipera latastei , sharing a haplotype with the historical specimen and clustering with modern populations from northeastern Iberia, validating its provenance and suggesting a single mitochondrial lineage since isolation. The extinct skink, Chalcides bedriagai , also shows affinities with eastern Iberia. These results point to a vicariant origin for the herpetofauna, likely isolated on the island following sea level rise after the Last Glacial Maximum. Conversely, a 2,600-year-old mouse incisor yielded a Mus musculus mitogenome, indicating Iron Age human-mediated introduction. Additionally, genomic analysis of a 11th-century CE human burial revealed an individual with genetic affinities to the Central Mediterranean and Balkans, highlighting medieval maritime mobility. This study resolves the long-debated Columbretes snake identity, traces biogeographic origins and illustrates the interplay of natural isolation and anthropogenic influence on the island biodiversity. research.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are key defence molecules of the innate immune system. Understanding the origins of AMPs can help to explain how immune systems acquire novelty and vary in their defence capacities. However, AMPs evolve rapidly, and so the origins of similar AMPs across organisms is often unclear. Furthermore, false negatives due to low search sensitivity are common and can hinder conaident annotations about true absences. As a result, understanding whether similar AMP genes found in diverse organisms represent ancestral molecules or evolutionary novelties has been challenging. Here, we present evidence of horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of the antifungal peptide gene Drosomycin across insects. We show that in Diptera, the presence of Drosomycin is restricted to the Drosophila Melanogaster species group and additionally the distant relative Drosophila busckii. We go on to recover Drosomycin genes in cockroaches (Blattodea), mantises (Mantodea), katydids (Orthoptera), beetles (Coleoptera), parasitic wasps (Hymenoptera), and a recently acquired and pseudogenized Drosomycin locus in Liposcelis booklice (Psocodea), but not other insects. Explaining this diversity through shared ancestry requires at least 60 independent loss events, or just nine HGT events. Previous studies have suggested that similar AMPs found across divergent species realect conservation from a common ancestor, or due to their small size, that they arose via convergent evolution. Our aindings suggest horizontal gene transfer can be responsible for the presence of some AMP genes scattered across the tree of life. By presenting a mechanism through which immune systems can acquire novelty, our study also suggests a possible explanation for certain lineage-speciaic defence competencies against infectious disease. While loss of AMP genes is well-documented, here we suggest gain of AMPs can occur just as suddenly.

research.abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is associated with altered outcomes in established prostate cancer, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We examined whether whole-body metabolic state and systemic metformin treatment are associated with changes in circulating plasma extracellular vesicle (EV) signaling to prostate cancer cells. Plasma EV-derived miRNAs were profiled in six T2D and six non-diabetic (ND) donors, selected mimics were tested in DU145 cells for effects on transcription of ZEB1 , a master regulator of tumor progression. Recipient cell transcriptional responses to human EV-enriched fractions were also assessed by RNA sequencing using six T2D and two ND donors. DU145 cells were also transfected with plasma EV-derived RNA from high fat diet (HFD)-fed mice with or without metformin treatment. Human miRNA profiling identified miR-192-5p, miR-106b-5p, and miR-29b-3p as candidates with greater than two-fold elevation and nominal P <0.05; none of the 84 assayed miRNAs remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Synthetic miR-192-5p and miR-106b-3p mimics increased ZEB1 , whereas miR-29b-3p had no effect on ZEB1 . T2D donor EV exposure was associated with broad range of aggressive responses, including cytoskeletal, extracellular matrix, mitotic, and RHO-GTPase-related pathways. Mouse EV-derived RNA from metformin-treated HFD mice induced lower DU145 migration than RNA from untreated HFD mice (12.23% versus 20.25% mean membrane coverage; n=3 mice/group; Welch P =0.0246). Matrigel invasion analysis showed less invasion for HFD+metformin than HFD alone (4.89% versus 7.89%; n=3 mice/group; Welch P =0.0302). These findings support a strong association between abnormal systemic metabolism and circulating EV signaling to drive prostate cancer progression, together with a metformin-driven reduction in the tumor progression activity of plasma EV-derived RNA. The responsible RNA species and molecular mechanisms will be central to future research.

research.abstract: Abstract The study of complex disorders is limited by the lack of structured data sets that integrate genetic association signals with rich functional annotations. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) provide large collections of associated variants, these are heterogeneous, study-dependent, and not directly suitable for machine learning applications. Although frameworks such as Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) offer comprehensive variant-level features, there is no standardised procedure to construct curated, balanced, and reproducible data sets for the systematic study of complex traits. We introduce a scalable and reproducible pipeline for generating CADD-annotated variant data sets associated with complex disorders defined via Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) terms. The pipeline integrates GWAS summary statistics, genome mapping, chromosome-stratified negative sampling, and large-scale annotation, while addressing class imbalance and feature redundancy. The resulting data sets provide curated, balanced, and annotation-rich representations of variant–trait associations, suitable for statistical learning, systematic model evaluation and comparison, and analysis of functional annotation contributions and interactions.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious pathogen globally despite decades of effective chemotherapy. In 2024, an estimated 10·7 million people developed tuberculosis, including approximately 620 000 people living with HIV (PLHIV), and tuberculosis caused an estimated 1·23 million deaths overall, including approximately 150 000 deaths among PLHIV. Men accounted for more than half of the cases, and children represented a substantial burden, reflecting ongoing transmission and diagnostic gaps. Approximately a quarter of the world's population has been infected with M tuberculosis, with immunological evidence of previous or current infection. This population includes groups at increased risk of progression to tuberculosis disease, particularly those with recent infection, HIV, undernutrition, young age, or other clinical and social vulnerabilities. Following 3 years of COVID-19-related setbacks, global tuberculosis incidence declined modestly (1%) from 2023 to 2024 but remains higher than in 2020 and far off-track to meet the 2025 WHO End TB Strategy milestones. Case detection improved to 8·3 million notifications (78% of estimated incident cases), supported by expanded molecular diagnostics; however, prevalence surveys continue to reveal substantial proportions of bacteriologically confirmed but asymptomatic tuberculosis, highlighting persistent transmission and missed diagnoses. 30 high-burden countries accounted for 87% of cases, led by India, Indonesia, the Philippines, China, Pakistan, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Bangladesh. M tuberculosis-HIV co-infection remains a major driver of mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Drug-resistant tuberculosis threatens progress: of 390 000 estimated multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis cases in 2024, only 42% initiated treatment, although treatment success improved to 71%. Tuberculosis-preventive treatment reached 5·3 million people, including 58% of PLHIV and 25% of eligible household contacts, well below global targets. Persistent undernutrition, poverty, HIV, diabetes, smoking, alcohol use, air pollution, migration, and conflict continue to shape tuberculosis epidemiology. With financing at only 27% of global targets, accelerated prevention, proactive case finding, social protection, and sustained political commitment are essential to eliminate tuberculosis.

research.abstract: In young animals, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in the CNS efficiently differentiate into myelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs), whereas ageing reduces this capacity, impairing remyelination following demyelinating injury and adaptive myelination involved in learning. To identify factors that restore resilience in aged OPCs, we developed gSWITCH ( https://altoslabs.shinyapps.io/gSWITCH/ , https://github.com/Tanay-math/gSWITCH ), a computational pipeline that captures dynamic gene-expression patterns to identify ‘switch’ genes during lineage progression and ordered biological transitions, including time-series experiments. gSWITCH identified OPC-characteristic switch genes, which we compared between young and aged OPCs to determine whether their regulation is altered with ageing. This revealed several transcription factors with reduced expression in aged OPCs. Transcription-factor binding-site enrichment highlighted Bcl11a as a potential master-regulator of multiple switch genes. Bcl11a inhibition reduced OPC differentiation into OLs, whereas its overexpression in aged OPCs significantly enhanced OL differentiation without affecting proliferation. In aged mice subjected to demyelination injury in spinal cord white matter, Bcl11a overexpression increased OPC differentiation within lesions. We found that Bcl11a has undergone pervasive purifying selection throughout vertebrate evolution, preserving its amino acid sequence by eliminating deleterious mutations. Our study shows that reversing the age-related decline of this evolutionarily conserved factor in aged OPCs restores their impaired capacity for differentiation.

research.abstract: Introduction Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical threat to global health security and disproportionately affects children in sub-Saharan Africa. In Nigeria, the burden of multidrug-resistant pathogens in paediatric populations is increasing; however, data from the South-South region, particularly Edo State, remain scarce. This study aims to determine the prevalence, patterns and transmission dynamics of AMR among paediatric patients in Edo State, Nigeria, using a One Health approach that integrates human, animal and environmental health interfaces. Methods and analysis This mixed-methods study will enrol 455 hospitalised children (<18 years) at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH). Clinical (urine, blood, rectal and nasopharyngeal swabs), environmental and animal samples will be collected to isolate and characterise locally recoverable bacterial pathogens prioritised with reference to the WHO 2024 priority pathogen list. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing will be performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method in accordance with Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Selected clinically or epidemiologically important resistant isolates will be stored at -80°C for possible future molecular characterisation, resources permitting. Key informant interviews with caregivers, healthcare providers and policymakers will explore the systemic enablers and barriers to paediatric AMR stewardship. Quantitative data will be analysed using descriptive statistics and logistic regression, while qualitative data will undergo thematic analysis guided by Braun and Clarke's framework. Ethics and dissemination Ethical approval has been obtained from the UBTH Health Research Ethics Committee (Ref: ADM/E 22/A/VOL.VII/14831247). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Findings will inform antibiotic stewardship, strengthen surveillance and guide AMR policy at institutional, state and national levels. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, policy briefs, institutional reports and engagement with national and international health agencies.

research.abstract: Abstract Background The vaginal microbiome is a key determinant of women’s health, with Lactobacillus -dominant communities protecting against bacterial vaginosis ( BV ) and related adverse outcomes. Dysbiosis involves a decline in lactobacilli and overgrowth of anaerobes, with Gardnerella species central to initiating polymicrobial aggregates. However, the genetic determinants of community assembly, biofilm formation, and interspecies interactions remain poorly understood. This study investigated the genomic and functional basis of these traits using an integrated multi-omics approach. Results Long-read whole-genome sequencing of clinical Gardnerella isolates yielded closed genomes and revealed a pangenomic split correlating with high-versus low-biofilm phenotypes, linked to clade-specific genomic islands and allelic variants. Functional gene modules within these regions distinguished G. vaginalis from G. piotii , contributing to nutrient acquisition, cell wall metabolism, and colonization. Integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and proteomics of all pairwise dual-species co-cultures of five key vaginal bacteria showed that G. vaginalis and L. iners acted as dominant ecological drivers, outcompeting neighbors and triggering asymmetric proteomic remodeling. Differential expression of a gene within a putative operon encoding a conserved type II secretion/Tad pilus system, revealed by integrating the pangenome with the proteome, implicated this system in interspecies interactions. AI-based structural predictions of the complex suggested isoform-specific differences in protein folding between G. vaginalis and G. piotii . In parallel, metagenomic analysis of 93 women showed the operon was more abundant in BV samples than in healthy controls, linking it to dysbiosis. Integrated metabolomics further identified a methyl-β-carboline compound elevated in Prevotella bivia -containing co-cultures that selectively inhibited G. vaginalis and P. bivia while sparing L. crispatus . Several dipeptides influenced growth and biofilm formation of vaginal microbes, and methyl-β-carboline and sphingosine additionally inhibited multidrug-resistant pathogens, suggesting new strategies for managing polymicrobial infections. Conclusions This work links Gardnerella genomic features to virulence-associated phenotypes and demonstrates how interspecies interactions shape community dynamics and antimicrobial metabolite production. The findings support a model in which biofilm capacity is genetically encoded within an accessory genome, deployed through tailored proteomic responses, and modulated by an interaction-specific metabolic landscape, providing a foundation for identifying bioactive molecules and developing diagnostics and targeted therapeutics to restore and maintain vaginal health. Highlights Long-read whole-genome sequencing of clinical Gardnerella isolates yielded closed ge-nomes and linked high-versus low-biofilm phenotypes to clade-specific genomic islands and allelic variants. Integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, proteomics, and metabolomics of all pairwise du-al-species co-cultures showed that Gardnerella vaginalis and Lactobacillus iners outcompete neighboring species and trigger asymmetric proteomic remodeling, identifying them as dominant ecological drivers of dysbiosis. AI-predicted structural variation in a conserved type II secretion/Tad pilus system, sup-ported by metagenomic cohort analysis of 93 women, distinguished healthy from dysbiotic states and highlights a candidate BV biomarker. Integrated metabolomics identified a methyl-β-carboline elevated in Prevotella bivia -containing co-cultures that selectively inhibits G. vaginalis and P. bivia while sparing L. crispatus , offering a narrow-spectrum therapeutic lead. Metabolites including several dipeptides modulated growth and biofilm of vaginal mi-crobes and multidrug-resistant pathogens, suggesting new strategies for managing polymicrobial infections

research.abstract: Mitochondrial genomes (mitogenomes) are no longer considered entities solely responsible for cellular bioenergetics, but as dynamic, multifaceted, and synchronized systems that integrate genome architecture, evolutionary processes, and organismal physiology. The present review summarizes the contemporary understanding of mitogenome organization and its diversity, evolution, and associated functions across eukaryotic life, with emphasis on mitonuclear co-evolution and relevance to human health. Moreover, the conserved and lineage-specific characteristics of mitogenome architecture, including its genetic content, topology, and regulatory elements, and their roles in governing the precise replication and transcription of the mitogenome are also comprehensively discussed. Additionally, the review explores the role of evolutionary dynamics, with emphasis on mutation-rate heterogeneity, recombination dynamics, gene rearrangements, and the interaction between mutation, natural selection, and genetic drift in shaping mitochondrial genome diversity and evolutionary trajectories. Comparative approaches have revealed extensive diversity in mitogenome structural organization and composition, which are closely associated with life-history traits of organisms, including metabolic rate, longevity, and reproductive characteristics. Notably, at the functional level, the variability potential of a mitogenome significantly influences oxidative phosphorylation efficiency, reactive oxygen species generation, and the orchestration of cellular signaling cascades. Fundamental to these processes is the existence of coordinated mitonuclear interrelationships, wherein coevolution between mitochondrial and nuclear-encoded genes safeguards bioenergetic functional integrity, whereas disruptions in this coordination may lead to reduced cellular fitness and progression of several diseases. Particularly in humans, mutations in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and heteroplasmy significantly contribute to the development of primary mitochondrial disorders and are increasingly implicated in other complex disease etiologies, including neurodegeneration, metabolic syndromes, and cancer. The paper also summarizes the phylogenetic utility of mitogenomes in the genomic era, accentuating the need to employ integrative approaches that combine mitochondrial and nuclear data. Lastly, the role of emerging technological platforms, including long-read sequencing and multi-omics, is also discussed, since these approaches are expected to transform the current landscape of mitogenome research. Altogether, the manuscript positions mitogenomes as indispensable entities bridging the gaps between evolutionary histories, physiological functions, and personalized precision medicine.

research.abstract: Background Toll-like receptor genes have been extensively researched for their role in the susceptibility to pulmonary tuberculosis across different populations. The relationship between variations in toll-like receptor genes and additional risk factors for pulmonary tuberculosis is not well understood, because of the complex interplay between genetic predispositions and environmental influences. This study aimed to elucidate the association of TLR2 T597C, TLR4 A896G, and TLR9 G1174A gene polymorphisms with the risk of developing pulmonary tuberculosis. Methods A total of 306 samples – 153 patients with pulmonary tuberculosis and 153 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were selected using a consecutive sampling technique. Clinical and biochemical variables were measured to assess the associated risk factors. Deoxyribonucleic acid was isolated from blood samples, and the TLR2 , TLR4, and TLR9 genotypes were identified using polymerase chain reaction–restriction fragment length polymorphism and analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis. Results Our analysis showed that the TLR2 -CC genotype (OR = 3.82; 95% CI = 1.79–8.16; P < 0.001) and C allele (OR=2.12; 95%CI: 1.42–3.10; P < 0.001), the TLR4 -GG genotype (OR=3.18; 95%CI: 1.71–5.92; P < 0.001) and G allele (OR=2.25; 95%CI: 1.61–3.14; P < 0.001), and the TLR9 -AA genotype (OR=2.00; 95%CI: 1.09–3.68; P = 0.025) and A allele (OR=1.60; 95%CI: 1.15–2.21; P < 0.001) is significantly associated in patients than in controls, suggesting their potential role as genetic risk factors for the development of pulmonary tuberculosis. Combined genotype analysis revealed that individuals carrying all three risk genotypes (CC-GG-AA) significantly associated with increased PTB risk. Multivariable analysis showed that HIV co-infection and malnutrition were independent predictors of pulmonary tuberculosis. Conclusion The TLR2 T597C gene of the CC genotype and the C allele, the TLR4 A896G genes of the GG genotype and the G allele, and the TLR9 G1174A genes of the AA genotype and the A allele are associated with increased risk of pulmonary tuberculosis among the Ethiopian patients under study.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Species in the Rosaceae tribe Spiraeeae occupy diverse habitats and vary strikingly in growth form and leaf morphology. Still, no reference transcriptomes have been published for the tribe, and its transcriptome‐level variation is uncharacterized. We generated long‐read (PacBio Iso‐Seq) reference transcriptomes of five species spanning three genera: Petrophytum caespitosum (Nutt.) Rydb., Spiraea lucida Douglas ex Greene, Spiraea splendens Baumann ex K. Koch, Aruncus dioicus (Walter) Fernald var. dioicus , and Aruncus aethusifolius (H.Lév.) Nakai. We then quantified expression across 20 individuals using 3′‐tag RNA sequencing (TagSeq) to characterize expression patterns, ortholog sequence divergence, and gene repertoire. Multivariate analyses (principal component analysis [PCA] and hierarchical clustering) resolved replicates into three groups corresponding to the sampled genera. Because the material combined field‐collected and potted plants, we treat expression comparisons as descriptive and do not attribute them to genetic control of interspecific differences. Pairwise analyses revealed extensive transcriptional divergence between genera, including thousands of differentially expressed transcripts in comparisons such as A. aethusifolius vs. P. caespitosum . Functional enrichment highlighted variation in transport and catabolism, plastid organization, and biotic‐stress responses, implicating both metabolic and organelle‐associated processes. Transcription factor families, particularly bHLH and bZIP, varied most among differentially expressed transcripts. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) recovered modules correlated with species identity; because between‐species variation dominates this dataset, we treat these as descriptive summaries of coexpression structure and do not regard them as independent evidence of species‐specific regulatory programs. Because reads were quantified against a reference assembled from species‐specific contigs, mapping rates were higher within species (70.5%–85.1%) than across species (25.1%–77.0%), and between‐species expression comparisons are interpreted with this asymmetry in mind. Sequence‐level analysis of orthologous transcript pairs indicated that protein‐coding genes are predominantly under purifying selection. A small fraction (2.7%–5.0% of retained pairs) showed Ka/Ks > 1, but these were concentrated at low synonymous divergence, where ratio estimates are unstable; we therefore treat them as screening‐level candidates for rapid divergence, enriched for stress‐response, membrane‐trafficking, and ion‐transport annotations, and we make no claim of positive selection. These results provide a comparative transcriptomic framework for Spiraeeae and identify candidate transcripts and protein‐coding differences for future studies of ecological and morphological variation in Rosaceae.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

research.abstract: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) contributes significantly to the global tuberculosis burden, yet treatment response and drug resistance remain poorly characterized. India, a high- tuberculosis burden country, faces growing challenges of delayed diagnosis, treatment and drug-resistant tuberculosis, particularly in extrapulmonary forms. This study evaluated early clinical response to therapy and identified factors associated with rifampicin resistance among patients with EPTB. A prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care centre in central India between 2018 and 2024. A total of 532 patients with microbiologically confirmed EPTB, based on the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, were included. The study collected baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory data. Clinical response at 8 weeks was assessed using standardized criteria. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified factors associated with slow clinical response and rifampicin resistance. A total of 5,764 presumptive EPTB samples were tested using the Xpert MTB/RIF assay. Among these, 532 patients had confirmed EPTB. Rifampicin resistance was detected in 36 patients (6.7%), while 496 patients had rifampicin-sensitive disease and were included in the response analysis. Among these patients, 113 (22.8%) demonstrated slow clinical response. Slow response showed independent association with HIV co-infection, diabetes mellitus, malnutrition, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, prolonged symptom duration, and non-lymph node disease, particularly abdominal and genitourinary tuberculosis. Socioeconomic factors, such as rural residence and lower educational status, also showed independent association. Elevated inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein, showed independent association with slow clinical response. Rifampicin resistance showed independent association with previous tuberculosis, HIV infection, male sex, and disseminated disease. A significant overlap existed between delayed clinical response and drug resistance, as rifampicin resistance occurred more frequently among slow responders than among responders (12.3% vs. 4.1%, p = 0.002). Nearly one-quarter of patients with EPTB demonstrated delayed clinical response at 8 weeks. Both host-related and disease-related factors showed association with treatment response, while rifampicin resistance showed strong association with prior tuberculosis and immunosuppression. The overlap between slow clinical response and drug resistance highlighted the importance of early molecular diagnostics and targeted clinical monitoring in high-risk patients.

research.abstract: Coupled Metropolis-Hastings MCMC sampling (runie-mcmc-skyline: G = 10,000 generations, 20% burn-in = 2,000 discarded, 8,000 posterior states) across 64 ancient/modern hominin mitogenomes and 16 nuclear loci (L = 87,227 *MAFFT / 86,612 Native Rust gotoh-msa aligned bp) resolving the 5-stage Neanderthal Ne(t) collapse (13,893 to 602.7 at 39.2 ka BP) and 37.3x speedup over *MAFFT + *IQ-TREE + *BEAST v1.10.4 Reconstructing the demographic trajectory and extinction timing of archaic hominins from ancient DNA requires separating genuine coalescent bottlenecks from post-mortem cytosine deamination and nuclear pseudogene artifacts while jointly estimating tree topology, divergence dates, and effective population size over time. Here we introduce and validate a configurable long-form Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler inside the Rust Native Inference Engine (runie-mcmc-skyline; default 10,000 generations with a 20% burn-in gate) and benchmark it against *BEAST, *IQ-TREE with *LSD2, and *PAML codeml across an 87,227-bp hominin alignment spanning Neanderthals, Denisovans, Sima de los Huesos, and modern humans. Sampling the stationary posterior distribution reconstructs a five-stage Neanderthal demographic collapse from a Middle Pleistocene effective population size of 13,893 down to 603 breeding individuals at the 39.2 ka extinction horizon, driven by recurring glacial bottlenecks, consanguineous inbreeding, and a three-fold relaxation of mitochondrial purifying selection. research.abstract: Phylogenetic trees are hybrid objects: branch lengths vary continuously, while topologies change discretely through edge contractions and expansions. Billera-Holmes-Vogtmann (BHV) tree space provides a canonical geometry for this structure, representing each resolved topology as a Euclidean orthant and topological changes as motion across shared lower-dimensional boundaries. We introduce PhylaFlow, a hybrid flow-matching model that learns posterior-basin transport in BHV tree space. PhylaFlow is trained on BHV geodesic paths from random starting trees to short-run posterior samples, coupling continuous branch-length motion within orthants with learned boundary events and discrete topology transitions. We evaluate the learned geometry operationally: if the flow reaches posterior-relevant regions, finite-budget Bayesian refinement initialized from, or guided by, its terminal trees should recover posterior-supported topologies more efficiently. Across DS1-DS8 phylogenetic posterior benchmarks, PhylaFlow substantially reduces initial Tree-KL relative to classical initializers. After finite-budget MrBayes refinement, direct PhylaFlow improves early and intermediate topology-recovery trajectories on most datasets, while split-guided PhylaFlow-MCMC obtains the strongest hard-case results. The best PhylaFlow variant outperforms short-warmup on seven of eight datasets and PhyloGFN on five of eight under the same refinement budget. In a joint sequence-conditioned experiment, sequence embeddings steer posterior split recovery, although exact posterior topology recovery remains preliminary. These results show that hybrid flow matching can learn actionable transport in BHV tree space and provide a geometry-aware proposal mechanism for Bayesian phylogenetic inference.

research.abstract: IntroductionCongenital portosystemic shunts (CPSS) are rare vascular malformations, with an estimated prevalence of 1/30000 live births, that cause portal blood to partly bypass the liver. CPSS frequently co-occur with congenital heart disease and other malformations, suggesting a shared developmental or genetic basis. Severe acquired clinical manifestations are present in a large proportion of patients with CPSS. Portopulmonary hypertension (PoPH), the most life-threatening, has been reported in as many as 7-14% of CPSS patients. Mounting evidence indicates that PoPH can arise early in life, particularly in children with CPSS, yet paediatric PoPH remains understudied. This project aims to identify genetic variants associated with PoPH in CPSS patients through whole-genomes, focusing primarily on known pathogenic genes for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), congenital heart disease (CHD), Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT), SNPs previously associated with PoPH in adults, and ultimately novel genomic variants. The overarching goal of the study is to improve personalised risk assessment and inform clinical decisions regarding elective shunt closure in individuals potentially at-risk of developing PoPH. Methods and analysisThe aim is to perform an international multi-centre exploratory genome analysis of patients with CPSS and PoPH identified through the International Registry of Congenital Portosystemic Shunts (IRCPSS). Whole-genome sequencing will be utilized to analyse both coding and non-coding regions in a predominantly paediatric cohort. Targeted analysis of established pathogenic genes associated with PAH, CHD, HHT, and PoPH will be complemented by a genome-wide approach to identify novel, potentially pathogenic variants, with variant classification assessed according to American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) criteria. Family-based analyses, including trio analyses and segregation studies, will enable the identification of dominant, recessive, and de novo variants, facilitating a comprehensive evaluation of variant inheritance pattern and pathogenic potential. Ethics and disseminationThis study has been approved by the CCER (Geneva cantonal ethics committee for research) and poses minimal risk to participants, limited to blood sampling performed as part of routine clinical care for patients. Genetic data will be securely stored and analysed in compliance with GDPR. Clinically significant findings will be communicated through recruiting physicians, in accordance with participant preference regarding incidental findings. Study results will be disseminated through open-access peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences to advance understanding and management of PoPH in individuals with CPSS and potentially other chronic liver diseases associated with portosystemic bypass. research.abstract: Abstract The ultraspeciose clade Otophysa — catfishes, carps, minnows, tetras, and their kin — accounts for most vertebrate diversity in modern freshwater ecosystems. However, a controversial assemblage of largely-fragmentary marine fossils has led some authors, most recently Liu et al., to advocate parallel freshwater invasions for this otherwise inland lineage. Here, we test this hypothesis under multiple sources of uncertainty. We provide the first phylogenetic analysis of the recently-named marine fossil genus † Sooinichthys , resolving it as sister to all modern otophysans. We also find that † Santanichthys , long treated as an early marine otophysan, lacks a Weberian apparatus and plausibly belongs outside Ostariophysi entirely. When increasing the taxon and marker sampling of Liu et al.’s genomic dataset, standardizing their ecological coding, accounting for alternative interpretations of important morphological characters, and applying a suite of biogeographic models, we find a marine origin in only 6 of 132 analyses, and only when enforcing fossil placements inconsistent with our own phylogenetic results. We contend that the parallel freshwater invasion hypothesis of otophysan diversification is an artifact of sparse taxon sampling, taphonomic biases, model selection errors, and fossil overinterpretation. The result is a cautionary case for inferences about the cradle of any ancient freshwater clade.

research.abstract: Abstract This perspective provides an overview of what we know from real-world data on reversal of drug resistance evolution. An important question for those who study drug resistance is whether it is possible to reverse the evolution of resistance, for example by halting the use of specific drugs for a patient or even a community or country. Evidence for successful reversal of resistance levels is spread out in many different subfields of infectious disease. I use examples from P. falciparum malaria, several bacterial species including E. coli, M. tuberculosis, and S. aureus, and the viral pathogen HIV, to show that it is possible to reverse the evolution of resistance.

research.abstract: Abstract Gene copy-number mutations are frequent and prevalent yet often overlooked. While initially considered to be the neutrally evolving raw material needed for the emergence of new genes through the process of gene duplication and divergence, recent technical advances and renewed interest start to unravel a fundamentally different picture for duplications in bacteria: rather than being neutral, duplications have strong direct and indirect fitness effects, and rather than giving rise to evolutionary novelty through protein family expansions, duplications allow to transiently simply make more of the same. Tandem duplications arise at frequencies orders of magnitude higher than single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), and they collapse at an even higher rate still. Understanding the biological idiosyncrasies of copy-number mutations is pivotal to understanding their fundamental role in bacterial evolution. Having multiple copies of a gene influences its evolutionary dynamics in surprising ways, slowing down divergence, acting along with purifying selection as a force of conservation, and facilitating “bet-hedging” in fluctuating environments or under diversifying selection. Paying careful attention to structural variation in genomic sequence analyses will yield a more comprehensive understanding of bacterial evolution, especially when it comes to the emergence of novel bacterial lineages, such as human pathogens.

research.abstract: Abstract Tuberculosis, an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis , remains endemic in regions where it is prevalent. Mycobacterium tuberculosis is an intracellular pathogen that can survive within host macrophages; however, the mechanisms governing its long-term persistence and the progression to active pulmonary tuberculosis remain poorly understood. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been implicated in the initiation and progression of numerous diseases. In our previous study, circRNA sequencing identified several circRNAs associated with tuberculosis progression. In the present study, sequencing and reverse transcription–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) analyses revealed that Circ_0074371 was significantly downregulated in monocytes from patients with active pulmonary tuberculosis (ATB) and was closely associated with disease onset and progression, exhibiting considerable diagnostic value for ATB. Functional experiments further showed that Circ_0074371 significantly impaired the intracellular survival of Mtb and promoted M1 macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, Circ_0074371 acted as a competing endogenous RNA by sequestering miR-4738-3p, a potent negative regulator of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation. Collectively, these findings identify Circ_0074371 as a tuberculosis-associated circRNA that regulates AMPK activity and reveal a novel mechanism through which Circ_0074371 influences macrophage polarization via the AMPK pathway, providing new insights into potential therapeutic targets for ATB.

research.abstract: Characium and Characium -like algae represent a taxonomically challenging group within Chlorophyceae. Due to their high phenotypic plasticity and convergent morphology, their true evolutionary relationships have long remained unresolved, and the lack of genomic resources has further hindered taxonomic revision. We sequenced and assembled seven complete chloroplast genomes from Characium and morphologically similar taxa and documented their detailed cell morphology. Comparative genomic analyses revealed that while most genomes retained the typical quadripartite structure, they exhibited significant structural variation, including gene rearrangements and diverse IR expansions/contractions. Furthermore, phylogenetic analyses based on 64 protein-coding genes successfully resolved the long-standing taxonomic ambiguity of Characium and Characium -like algae, placing the strains into three distinct, well-supported clades within Sphaeropleales and Volvocales. The synteny patterns and DCJ distances were consistent with the phylogeny: closely related species showed largely conserved gene order and low DCJ distances, whereas more distant lineages exhibited extensive rearrangements and higher distances. Branch-site tests identified a small set of positively selected genes, mainly related to photosynthesis, proteolysis, and plastid gene expression, suggesting that adaptive processes may have contributed to chloroplast genome diversity in these algae. This study establishes the first clear phylogenomic framework for these lineages, revealing distinct evolutionary patterns of gene loss and structural rearrangement that align with the newly resolved clades. It also provides an important basis for advancing studies on chloroplast genome evolution within Chlorophyceae.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Insomnia (INS) is a major factor determining the risk, severity, treatment resistance and relapse of depression (DEP) and anxiety disorders (ANX), suggesting shared neurobiological vulnerability. Identifying common biological mechanisms that are therapeutically actionable is a foundational step towards improving current clinical care. Since INS, DEP, and ANX share substantial genetic risk, pinpointing the specific genetic factors that influence these three conditions simultaneously offers a route to discover pharmacological targets with transdiagnostic potential. Methods We propose a framework of multi-level trivariate genetic analysis to identify the shared genetic component of INS, DEP and ANX using genome-wide association studies (GWAS). We trace shared components through trivariate genetic overlap, local genetic correlations, overlapping genome-wide significant loci, shared predicted effector genes, and shared putative causal variants. Results We show that INS, DEP and ANX share 55% of their GWAS signal. We identify 195 cross-disorder loci, many of which are likely arising from the same causal variant (at least 50%) or predicted effector gene (60-80%). We find convergence of shared predicted effector genes on biological processes such as inhibitory synaptic transmission, neuronal organization, and axonal development. The majority of shared predicted effector genes that are also druggable are involved in synaptic transmission and located in synaptic membranes, nominating CACNA2D3, DRD2, GRIA1 and GRM5 as key targets for drug development to treat comorbid INS, DEP and ANX. Conclusion These results reveal an interconnected but mechanistically diverse basis for shared genetic liability across co-occurring INS, DEP and ANX, and offer potential candidates for future pathway-tailored transdiagnostic therapeutic targets.

research.abstract: Purpose Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) covers multiple drug resistance-associated regions, but drug-organized reports can duplicate variants across drugs and disperse a patient's variants. Through nomenclature standardization and cross-drug deduplication, we reconstructed nonredundant patient-level variant profiles and characterized multigene co-occurrence, molecular variant complexity, and reported frequency patterns. Patients and methods This single-center retrospective descriptive study included each patient's earliest eligible mutation-positive tuberculosis tNGS report from 2024-2025. The analysis dataset comprised report-derived information and did not include raw sequencing data or systematically paired phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST) results. Variants were standardized using the 2023 World Health Organization catalogue, H37Rv coordinates, and Human Genome Variation Society recommendations. Duplicate patient-gene-variant records were collapsed into unique patient-variant events while retaining drug annotations. Eight mutually exclusive, exhaustive combinations were defined from RIF (rpoB), INH (katG and/or inhA), and FQ (gyrA and/or gyrB) axes. Results Fifty-seven patients contributed 180 unique patient-variant events involving nine genes and 56 standardized variants. rpoB (84.2%) and katG (64.9%) were the leading genes. The leading variants were katG p.Ser315Thr (63.2%), rpsL p.Lys43Arg (29.8%), and rpoB p.Ser450Leu (26.3%), which together accounted for 37.8% of all events; 33 of 56 variants occurred in only one patient. Seven of the eight RIF/INH/FQ combinations were observed. RIF+/INH+/FQ- was most common (31/57, 54.4%), whereas RIF+/INH+/FQ+ had the highest median numbers of genes and variants (both 5.0). Twenty-three events in 16 patients had reported frequencies below 100%, and pncA- and gyrA-associated events accounted for 60.9%. Conclusion In this mutation-positive cohort, patient-level reconstruction integrated annotations of the same variant across drugs and characterized hotspots and a long tail of variants, multigene co-occurrence within RIF/INH/FQ combinations, and report-derived frequency patterns. This traceable data structure may support laboratory report review and future genotype-phenotype studies.

research.abstract: Abstract Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus), once a minor by-catch in the East China Sea, has bloomed into a dominant species, altering marine ecosystems. This study explored the genomic basis of its mysterious recent success via chromosome-level genome assembly, comparative and population genomics. The genome assemblies of H. nehereus and its closely related outgroup species Saurida undosquamis were of good quality, showing a 96.7–96.8% Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologues completeness. Population resequencing supports a single panmictic population throughout the coast of China. Expanded gene families and genes under intensified and positive selection are related to osmoregulation, hypoxia tolerance, immune function and reproduction. Recent selective sweeps are mostly related to immune response. These molecular signatures are consistent with long-term adaptations to a hypoxic, polluted and fluctuating environment. These findings suggest that species genomically preadapted to environments affected by global change can suddenly become new native invaders.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is one of the most common and prognostically relevant valvular heart diseases, with a growing global burden driven by population ageing. Prediction of disease progression from moderate to severe AS, which would be instrumental for earlier diagnosis and treatment, remains challenging. At the same time, moderate AS is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition associated with clinically relevant risk, particularly in patients with cardiac damage, heart failure, or rapid disease progression. Conventional echocardiographic parameters incompletely capture the biological heterogeneity underlying AS progression. The MODAS study was established to investigate biomarkers and mechanisms of AS progression and outcome using longitudinal multimodal phenotyping. Methods The MODAS Study is a prospective, multicenter, longitudinal observational cohort study enrolling adults with moderate calcific tricuspid AS at three tertiary heart valve centers in Germany. Participants undergo standardized baseline assessment including clinical phenotyping, laboratory testing, electrocardiography, transthoracic echocardiography, cardiac computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Biospecimens are collected for biomarker, immunologic, proteomic, and genetic analyses, including genome-wide association studies and assessment of clonal haematopoiesis. Participants are followed annually for up to 5 years with repeat clinical assessment, laboratory testing, and echocardiography. The primary endpoint is time to progression to severe AS according to 2025 ESC/EACTS guideline criteria or aortic valve replacement for severe AS, adjudicated by the local multidisciplinary Heart Team. Secondary endpoints include all-cause mortality and additional clinical outcome trajectories. Multimodal data integration will be used to develop and validate prediction models for disease progression and outcome. Discussion The MODAS Study will provide a harmonized, deeply phenotyped longitudinal dataset to improve risk stratification in moderate AS and to identify imaging, inflammatory, and genetic markers associated with rapid progression and adverse outcomes. The study is designed to support future personalized surveillance strategies, improved selection for earlier intervention, and mechanistic understanding of calcific AS progression. research.abstract: Abstract Background Effective type 2 diabetes (T2D) education improves patient outcomes, but clinician time constraints limit what can be covered during encounters. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable way to answer patient questions, yet their accuracy and reliability in T2D education across health literacy levels remain poorly characterized. Methods We developed DiaBench, a standardized benchmarking framework built from 96 question- and-answer pairs collected by clinicians from representative real-world patient encounters. GPT-5 transformed each pair into multiple-choice questions (MCQs) under three configurations (1-3) simulating different question formats and levels of user background. A five-member panel of certified diabetes care and education specialists (CDCESs), medical doctors (MDs), and endocrinologists validated the transformations, rating question rephrasing, answer rephrasing, and answer correctness. We then evaluated seven LLMs (GPT-5 1 , Gemini-2.5-Flash 2 , Cohere Command 3 , Llama-4 4 , DeepSeek-R1 5 , Perplexity Sonar 6 , Mistral-Large-2.0 7 ) for accuracy and self-consistency across three runs. Results (i) Expert validation showed a consensus over MCQ transformation. For configuration 1, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of rephrased answers were appropriate, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of MCQ answers were correct, and 95.0% (SD 0.05) of rephrased questions were appropriate; corresponding values for configuration 2 were 96.3% (SD 0.05), 97.5% (SD 0.02), and 89.8% (SD 0.14). (ii) across benchmarking for configurations 1 and 2, most models achieved high accuracy (≥95%), but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models (≥95%). All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3. Conclusions DiaBench quantitatively differentiates LLM capability in T2D patient education, with Gemini, GPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 performing strongly and other models suboptimally. DiaBench provides a transferable platform for evaluating existing and newly developed LLMs, addressing the need for standardized benchmarking before clinical deployment of LLM-based systems in patient education.

research.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global public health concern, with Gram-negative carbapenem-resistant bacteria (CRG) classified by WHO as critical priority pathogens. Biomedical waste disposal sites (BMWs) may act as reservoirs for resistant organisms, posing occupational and community risks. This study investigated the phenotypic and genotypic characterization of Gram-negative carbapenem resistant bacteria in bioaerosols collected from BMW facilities in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. Bioaerosols were sampled using active Six-stage Andersen Impactors and passive settled plates. Isolates were identified by MALDI-TOF, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST). Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed for 26 representative isolates, and resistance gene profiling was conducted using CARD and ResFinder databases. Representative isolates belonged to Moraxellaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Pseudomonadaceae families. All species showed resistance to linezolid, and approximately 60% were multidrug resistant to carbapenems, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones. Genotypic analysis confirmed the prevalence of carbapenemase genes, with blaNDM-1 most frequent, followed by blaNDM-7, blaVIM-2, blaVIM-11, blaOXA-23, and blaOXA-235. This is the first report documenting Acinetobacter baumannii, A. schindleri, A. towneri, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas juntendi in bioaerosols from BMW sites. Biomedical waste environments serve as critical reservoirs of AMR. These findings emphasize the need for surveillance, protective measures, and integration of environmental AMR monitoring into public health policy.
